findings.trigger_condition: Input contains many distinct unhashable node values (e.g. lists). Each new unhashable value hashes with TypeError and is looked up by linear equality scan of every previously registered node: first unhashable_ids then hashable_ids, O(V) per lookup, O(V^2) overall.
findings.root_cause: The unhashable branch of _id_of performs a full linear equality scan of all registered nodes on every lookup because unhashable values cannot be indexed. Measured scaling confirms quadratic behavior: 2k-node unhashable chain 0.24s, 5k 1.47s, 10k 5.86s, 20k 23.3s (≈4x time per 2x input).
findings.impact: A 50k-100k node input of unhashable values takes minutes (est. ~150s at 50k, ~10min at 100k). Any hidden performance test with a large unhashable graph, or the contract's 'very deep acyclic inputs' requirement exercised with unhashable values, will time out. Hashable-only inputs are unaffected (500k chain in 1.01s).
findings.suggested_validation: Time dependency_layers on a 50k-100k deep chain of unhashable node values (e.g. [[i] for i in range(N)]) with a realistic timeout and compare against the reference implementation's runtime.

findings.trigger_condition: Workload contains U unhashable nodes registered early plus H hashable node lookups, even when no cross-type equality actually exists. Every hashable lookup scans the entire unhashable_ids registry (O(U)), making the fast path O(H*U) total.
findings.root_cause: The hashable fast path always cross-checks every registered unhashable node to support equality across hashability boundaries, regardless of whether the new value's type could possibly compare equal to an unhashable entry. Measured: U=100/H=50k -> 0.67s, U=500/H=50k -> 2.96s, U=1000/H=100k -> 11.55s (linear in H*U).
findings.impact: A mixed test with e.g. 50k hashable + 2k unhashable nodes costs ~100M equality comparisons (~10s+); 500k hashable + 5k unhashable costs billions (~minutes). This is the dominant cost of mixed large inputs and can TLE hidden tests even though correctness is preserved.
findings.suggested_validation: Benchmark dependency_layers with a chain of a few thousand unhashable nodes followed by ~100k hashable node lookups (no cross-type equality) and compare total runtime against a reference that skips the cross-check when value types cannot match.

findings.trigger_condition: A node value whose __eq__ returns a non-bool (e.g. numpy array) or raises (e.g. __eq__ raising TypeError instead of returning NotImplemented), or whose __hash__ raises a non-TypeError exception.
findings.root_cause: _same_node uses 'left is right or left == right' and truthiness of the == result without containing exceptions; hash(value) at line 57 only catches TypeError. Any non-bool comparison result (numpy arrays raise ValueError: ambiguous truth value) or raising __eq__/__hash__ propagates out of dependency_layers mid-iteration.
findings.impact: dependency_layers crashes on such node types instead of either treating them as distinct nodes or raising a clean error, and the one-shot iterable is abandoned mid-stream. Only affects exotic node types; plain Python objects are unaffected.
findings.suggested_validation: Feed node values with array-like __eq__ (e.g. a wrapper returning a list from __eq__) and confirm whether the evaluator's inputs can include such types; if so, the == call needs a bool() guard and exception containment.
